notes.title: How to Report Toxic Players
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/12164976/941bca2306c48743aca598ead162ec725eb3289e.jpg[/img]


[h1]DON'T LET TROLLS RUIN YOUR FUN[/h1]
As our game continues to grow, we’re continuously working to help foster a healthy and positive community. Robot takes the player experience very seriously and we have no interest in letting toxic players ruin the fun of the game for anyone else (see our [url=https://orcsmustdie.com/#!/en/code-of-conduct]Code of Conduct[/url] for details). Let’s talk a little bit about how reports from players contribute to the community we are growing!

We receive reports every day from community members with their concerns about other players. These reports help us sort through the data on our end to identify toxic situations. Each report is carefully reviewed and we seek out additional information in our systems to flesh out the details. Every report is reviewed by multiple team members so that we can make an accurate decision consistent with our policies.


[h1]HOW DO I REPORT A PLAYER?[/h1]
If you see a player that is violating the [url=https://orcsmustdie.com/#!/en/code-of-conduct]Code of Conduct[/url], [url=https://orcsmustdie.com/#!/en/acceptable-use]Acceptable Use Policy[/url], or the [url=https://orcsmustdie.com/#!/en/terms-of-service]Terms of Service[/url] in some way, you can and should report their activity directly to Robot Entertainment. Posting in the forums is nice, but there's a chance it may get missed. For that reason, we only handle player reports directly through our ticketing system.

To report a player, fill out a Support Ticket [url=http://support.robotentertainment.com/hc/en-us/requests/new]here[/url]. When submitting your report, always remember that the more information you can give us, the better. Be sure to include details like your in-game nickname, the nickname of the player you're reporting, screenshots, the date and approximate time of the incident you're reporting, and what happened. You can find more information on how to provide a detailed report [url=http://support.robotentertainment.com/hc/en-us/articles/202499899]here[/url].


[h1]WHAT HAPPENS AFTER I REPORT A PLAYER?[/h1]
It’s important to note that player privacy is a major concern. If you’re reporting a player, that player isn’t told who reported them. Similarly, if a player’s actions have warranted some kind of action, we keep that information private as well. Punishment is generally a break from the game. Publically shaming that person would be a further punishment that we do not feel is right. 

While results are kept private, we can tell you we take each report seriously. Since you’ve spent the time to write up all the details of the situation, it’s only fair that we’re thorough in checking it out. Players that violate the code of conduct receive a suspension that matches with the severity of the offense. As long as you’ve provided an accurate report of someone violating the code of conduct, you can assume action was taken.

Suspending a player isn’t something we take lightly.We understand some players plan their day around their gaming time, and not being able to play your favorite game is a serious change in plans. However, we simply cannot tolerate players creating a toxic experience for others. 

OMD!U is all about killin’ orcs and smashin’ dorks. The goal is to have fun with your friends while the green things get gibbed. We appreciate everyone’s help growing our community!

notes.title: Bloodspike Unchained: Release 1.2 Now Available!
notes.notes:
Toward the end of Closed Beta, we revamped the entire crafting system in Orcs Must Die! Unchained, and while we were really happy with the results, Open Beta players had a clear message for us – they want more control. And it wasn’t just crafting. Players have been looking for more power and control over their game experience in several areas. On every episode of Insider Access, in tons of forum posts, and in every survey, we’ve made promises to listen to your feedback and make changes based on it.

[h1]We're turning your feedback into features.[/h1]

Release 1.2 represents some of our biggest community feedback-driven changes to date. There’s a lot in this release, but here’s a look at some of the biggest changes that affect your questions and concerns about the state of the Open Beta.
[list][*][b]Survival of the Fittest[/b] - With every new update, Survival mode feels more and more like the classic Orcs Must Die! gameplay you fell in love with. Now, minions move faster and take more damage from your assaults. Hero damage bonuses make your weapons hit harder and your magic pack more punch. Minion waves on all Survival battlegrounds are rebalanced to be more exciting for new players and to give high-level players greater challenges to overcome.  To top it all off, the new Banquet Hall Survival battleground is the most compact OMD2-like map we’ve ever released. We’re keeping PvP Siege mode on an even playing field, but planning even more adjustments and updates to PvE Survival to give you that classic OMD feeling.

[/*][*][b]Craft What You Want[/b] - Crafting has been beaten into submission. The number of materials is sliced in half and recipes were thrown into the blade walls to make the entire crafting system bow to your every whim. No more hoping for the best from random drops. Choose the materials you want to pursue for the cards you want to craft, then go earn them on the battlefield! Target the rewards you actually need and craft new traps, traits, heroes, and minions with reckless abandon.

[/*][*][b]Become a Trap God[/b] - Every trap in the game now has seven upgrade tiers instead of four, so you can upgrade your traps more frequently. Build your highly-customized Survival mode deck of dastardly murder contraptions to inflict pain on unsuspecting enemy minions just the way you like. You’ll also start upgrading your traps even sooner than before, with upgrades unlocking now at level 10 instead of 25. When you put it all together, that means that there are no safe words allowed in your killbox – only pain.

[/*][*][b]Bloodspike Returns[/b] – One of our most powerful heroes in the game arrives in Release 1.2. With a murderous new set of abilities, Bloodspike the Brutal joins the thirteen heroes already warring for the rifts in Orcs Must Die! Unchained. With so many heroes to choose from, and many more on the way, there’s a powerful option for every attacker, pillager, and defender on your team.

[/*][/list]

notes.title: Prepare to be Brutal
notes.notes:
The Unchained's most fearsome warlord has escaped from the dungeons of Frostbite Fortress. He's not happy, and no one will stand in his way this time. [b]Beware; Bloodspike, the Brutal, is coming[/b].

[url=https://orcsmustdie.com/#!/en/blog/prepare-to-be-brutal][img]https://cdn.orcsmustdie.com/content/WebsiteCDN/blog/prepare-to-be-brutal/bloodspike_blog-header.jpg[/img][/url]

Bloodspike is infamous as the most feared commander of the Unchained forces, not only because of his success on the battlefield but for the cruelty and brutality of his methods of motivating his forces. He was recently sent by the orcish matriarch Bionka to capture Eventide Fortress. Tundra was able to repel the assault and Bloodspike was captured and imprisoned by the grizzlies. 

Bloodspike is a frontline leader who thrives off of the thrill of battle and spectacle of the carnage. He is at his best when escorting large armies that can fuel his abilities and his appetite. Bloodspike motivates his troops and strengthens his attacks through pain and fear, beating on his own minions to power his abilities. In order to maintain his attack, he is known to eat the flesh of his fallen men to keep his strength and ensure his orders are obeyed. From a playstyle standpoint, he is strongest when he stays with his minions and uses them to power up his abilities. He can then unleash devastating attacks when opponents approach the minion wave he is leading.

[b][url=https://orcsmustdie.com/#!/en/blog/prepare-to-be-brutal]Read the full hero preview with Lead Hero Designer Paul Hellquist[/url][/b], and prepare yourself for Bloodspike the Brutal!

Centuries ago, the grizzlies pleaded for the Order's help in defending their lands against a massive orc invasion. notes.title: Hotfix 4.1.2016
notes.notes:
War Mages!

With the number of games and new players we have now, we’re getting a lot of actionable data and feedback (thanks). We’ve started tuning.

Matchmaking has generally improved with the last few rounds of changes, but there are some new wrinkles.

In Survival Mode (PvE), we are seeing fast games with players of similar level ranged but also smaller team sizes. This is because we had some aggressive settings there. We’re going to loosen these a bit, allowing the matcher to search for a slightly longer time – this should produce games with full teams more often. (Note that, for survival, we adjust content to suit the number of players, so if you get in game with less than five players, the game will tweak things to suit your party.)

In Siege Mode (PvP), we are seeing far more drops at the hero selection and far more games canceled by a player who does not ready up when a match is found. There’s a problem with removal of players who do not accept matches, meaning that one absentee player cycles through multiple times ruining multiple games – this is getting fixed now and will be live soon.

Some players were apparently trying to complete some of the “play 10 games as” quests and dropping when they didn’t get the correct hero. We’ve since replaced these with a hero neutral “win five games” quest so that that motivation isn’t there. If a player had one of the old quests, it’ll still be valid until they complete it, so this change will take a little while to filter.

Siege was also seeing some good groups of players that were assigned to teams in bad ways. We have changed the algorithm so that it does a better job of creating the fairest possible teams.

On rewards, one of the things we’re seeing (both in numbers and comments) is that some of our rewards aren’t working as intended. In a few places, there are just errors, but in others things aren’t working as we intended. We are tuning this (and please expect more tuning in the weeks to come).

One of our main issues is that there are parts of this that are missing. For example, you don’t have a good way to steer yourself toward rewards with consistent progress (to say “I want this trap, so I’ll do X to earn it”) and you don’t have a way to exchange stuff you don’t want for stuff you do want. Some new parts will be happening, but we’re going to tweak things to improve this while we’re waiting.

One of the big issues right now is the hero chase. We recently eliminated all of the quest rewards except for skulls or rift embers, which is intended to make it easier to earn a hero. We’re also going to adjust early level up rewards to include rift embers so that players can work toward unlocking heroes. (For players who have already leveled up, we’ll be going back and granting the embers you would have earned.)

The hero recipes were also all set to a baseline and had not been adjusted. If you look at the store, you’ll see we offer heroes at different prices but the recipes do not have this same spread. That’s being adjusted and will be in after the next update.

Trap upgrades and parts are in a similar boat – these are also getting a look and I expect tuning there too.

Thanks for playing!

Reminder: this announcement pertains to the North American service only. Please stay tuned for updates to the European service from the Gameforge team!

notes.title: Hotfix 3.30.2016
notes.notes:
Attention War Mages:

Thank you all for your feedback and participation in the OMDU open beta! Over the first day, we’ve collected a lot of great data and feedback (thanks). Based on what we’ve been seeing, some changes were rolled out this afternoon at roughly 5 p.m. CST on the North American Service. 

[b]Survival Matchmaking[/b]
We allow a large span of account levels to match together and the random level selection has freedom to pick maps from above or below the average level of the party. This is causing a number of games where higher level players get matched with lower level players and then end up defending against hordes of orcs far below their level. A lot of players have commented about not feeling challenged when this happens.[list][*][b]We have lowered the allowed range, which will mean more players of similar levels get matched together.[/b][*][b]We have allowed survival games to match with fewer than five players[/b] instead of putting players with very different levels together just to make a five player group. (The difficulty adjusts, so if you get in a three player group, you’re fighting attackers meant for a three player group.)[*][b]We have changed the maps that can be selected to exclude maps below the average party account level. [/b]You’ll always get something at or slightly higher than the party’s average account level.[/list]

[b]Siege Matchmaking[/b]
As far as we can tell, everyone on the planet hates getting games with bots (not the good kind, I mean). We did this, and also had two matchmaking buckets, to try to give new players a better introductory experience. But, what we’re seeing and hearing makes us think we’re doing more harm than good.

[b]We have killed the buckets and the bots along with them and test how this plays out.[/b] So (for the time being) -- everyone looking for a siege game will search together and you will never get bots.

[b]Rift Embers[/b]
Everyone wants to earn the heroes they don’t have. This requires rift embers. You can get rift embers in a lot of different ways, but only a few of these are guaranteed. That makes working toward a hero frustrating. [i]We have a number of improvements in the works to allow earning materials and such to be more guided but we wanted to get a change in for this quickly.[/i]

[b]For now we've dropped all other rewards for the quests aside from skulls and rift embers. [/b]There were a lot of other rewards there before – all of them except for skulls and embers will go away. This means that, for heroes, players will always have a guaranteed way to make progress.

This is not ideal or the full solution, but this change can be made right now and will make things better (we hope). Note – if you already have quests, they’ll remain with the old rewards. If you decline these quests(the “x” in the upper right), you’ll get new ones with the skull or ember rewards. (You can only decline one quest per day.)

Thanks again for all of the games, data, feedback, chats,emails, and so on – we’re cranking on a lot of things that will make you happy.

OMDU is currently in Open Beta. We’re listening to you. Please check out [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/427270/discussions/1/]our forums[/url] and let us know how we can make the game better for you.
